title: Sloppy Joes with Tangy Tomato Beef on Toasted Buns
summary: Beef mince is tenderised with a little bicarbonate, browned with onion, garlic, paprika and tomato purée, then simmered with ketchup, cider vinegar and mustard until thick.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Tenderise the beef
steps.text: Stir the bicarbonate into 1 tbsp water, then mix it and the salt into the beef. Leave for 10 minutes; this keeps the mince tender and juicy.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, sugar, paprika and chilli flakes for 30 seconds, then the tomato purée, cooking for 2 minutes until it darkens.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Add the beef, breaking it into small pieces, and cook for 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Whisk the ketchup, vinegar, mustard, cornflour and 200 ml water together. Stir into the pan and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to mound on a spoon and the beef reaches 71 °C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Toast the cut sides of the buns in a dry pan for 1 minute. Spoon a quarter of the beef onto each base, add pickles and the lid.

tips: Taste before serving and add a splash more vinegar if you like it sharper.
The mixture thickens as it stands, so add a spoonful of water if it gets too stiff.
Freeze any extra filling for a quick weeknight dinner.
storage: Refrigerate the filling within 1 hour for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
